sentences.text:
The present revision petition under Sections 438/442 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (hereinafter "BNSS") read with Sections 397/401 of the Code of the Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter "CrPC"), on behalf of the petitioner/revisionist, has been filed seeking setting aside of the judgment dated 14.07.2025, passed in CRL.
APPEAL No. 299/2023 by the learned ASJ, vide which judgement on conviction dated 23.08.2023 and order on sentence dated 13.09.2023, passed by the learned JMFC in CR.
CASE No. 56625/2016 arising out of FIR No. 734/2000 was upheld.
2. List in due course.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/11/2025 at 22:56:38 CRL.M.(BAIL) 1967/2025 (Suspension of sentence)
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner/applicant submits that the applicant has been convicted under Sections 420/471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter "IPC") and consequently has been awarded sentence of simple imprisonment for a period of one year along with fine of Rs. 500/- for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC and simple imprisonment for a period of one year along with the fine of Rs. 500/- for the offence punishable under Section 471 of the IPC.

All sentences shall run concurrently Vijay Kumar Jain vs State Nct Of Delhi And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93711176/

sentences.text: It is submitted that the present application has been filed under Sections 438(1)/528 of the BNSS read with Sections 397(1)/482 of the CrPC seeking suspension of the sentence and for petitioner's release on regular bail till the final disposal of the instant criminal revision petition.

5. It is submitted that the impugned judgment has been challenged on grounds that (i) the alleged forgery relied upon by the prosecution is only a photocopy, no original was ever proved in Court,
and (ii) even as per the scientific report, the signature on the questioned document is not that of the applicant.
6.
It is further submitted that as per the nominal roll, out of the total sentence of one year, the applicant has already undergone incarceration for a period of almost three months and eight days.

It is urged that considering that the sentence is only of one year (simple imprisonment) and that the present revision petition is likely not to come up for hearing in the near future, therefore, if he is kept confined during pendency, the revision itself will become infructuous.
7. The applicant has no previous criminal antecedents, is a senior citizen This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/11/2025 at 22:56:38 of age 68 years with co-morbidities, and his jail conduct is recorded as satisfactory.
The applicant was on bail during the trial and there is no allegation of misuse of liberty at any earlier point as the applicant never misused the concession of bail.
The applicant has deep roots in the society, is a resident of Delhi and undertakes to abide by any condition that this Court may impose.

8. In the circumstances such as the short sentence, the period already undergone, the absence of any misuse, and in view of the settled principle of law that fixed-term sentences up to three years are ordinarily to be suspended unless exceptional circumstances exist, the applicant humbly prays that his sentence be suspended during pendency of the present petition.

9. Heard.
10.

Learned counsel appearing for the State vehemently opposed the present application for suspension of sentence submitting to the effect that the impugned judgment has been passed in accordance with the law and there is no illegality of any kind thereto.
11. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record 12.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sudhir Kumar Jain v. State of Delhi (MANU/SC/8988/2007),
observed that Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (now Section 430 of the BNSS)
empowers the Appellate Courts to suspend sentences till the pendency of appeal where period of sentence does not exceed 3 years.

Legislature, in its wisdom, has enacted Section 389, Code of Criminal Procedure Sub-section (3) of which empowers the Trial Court to suspend the sentence of such convicts, who have been convicted for a period not exceeding three years, for such period as will afford them sufficient time to present an appeal.

Section 389 also empowers the Appellate Court including the High Court to suspend the sentence and release the convict on bail during the pendency of the appeal in case the period of sentence does not exceed three years."
13. Most recently, the Supreme Court has reiterated and applied this very approach in Aasif @ Pasha v. State of U.P., 2025 INSC 944.

entities.text: Aasif @ Pasha v. State of U.P., 2025 INSC 944
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dealing with a four-year fixed-term sentence, the Hon'ble Court corrected the High Court for refusing suspension, emphasized that appeals are unlikely to be heard promptly, and directed that fixed-term sentences be suspended "liberally unless there are exceptional circumstances".
The Court also reminded that reasons must be recorded, and that the inquiry at this stage is limited.

14. At the same time, it is to be kept in mind that post-conviction suspension stands on a different footing from pre-trial bail, and that appellate courts must not re-appreciate the entire evidence when considering suspension of sentence.
15. In the present case, the applicant has been convicted effectively for a fixed term of one year.
Further, he remained on bail throughout investigation and trial, and has not misused liberty; he is a senior citizen with ailments; and he has deep social roots and a fixed residence.
These facts are borne out from the record placed with the instant application and diminish any risk of absconding or non-attendance, when the revision petition is finally heard.

16. Considering that the effective sentence awarded to the applicant is imprisonment for a period of one year, this Court deems it appropriate to suspend the sentence of the applicant during the pendency of the revision petition.
